newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Mubarak discuss reviving Syria talks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Mubarak discuss reviving Syria talks.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Monday that he and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak had agreed to seek ways to try to revive the Syrian-Israeli track of the Middle East peace process.

"We had a very long, good, detailed discussion about what we might do together to get the Syrian negotiations back on track and we both agreed now to go out and do a few things to see if we can make that happen," Clinton told a news conference after meeting Mubarak at the White House.

Clinton, with Mubarak at his side, added: "Whether we can, of course, is up to President (Hafez al-) Assad and Prime Minister (Benjamin) Netanyahu but we believe it's important. We believe there is at least a potential there that the parties could reach out across the ground that divides them."
Talks between Syria and Israel were suspended last year before Netanyahu took power, but he has subsequently taken a tougher line than the previous government.

Mubarak said it was vital to get the Syrian track resumed and said he had discussed this with both Assad and Netanyahu. "It is my earnest hope that we can work out an acceptable formula for the resumption of talks with the help of the United States," Mubarak said.

Damascus says it is willing to resume the talks as long as they start from where they left off, a position supported by Mubarak at Monday's news conference, but Israel refuses to accept what it considers preconditions. European powers are also trying to get the stalled talks going again.
